lessons.title: नाम (nām) — the first A1 form label

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Read the known word नाम (nām). Say what it means, then write it once from the word you already know.

blocks.title: You'll want to know first — read the label

segments.text: On a form, नाम (nām) asks for a name. The colon belongs to the form; it is not a Devanagari letter. Point to the label, then point to the empty answer line.

Copy only नाम (nām) once. Check न, then ा, then म, and draw each head-line after its letter shape. Do not add a value yet. This visible copy is supported script practice, not independent form writing.
Find नाम (nām) among काम, नाम (nām), दाम without writing the other words.

segments.prompt: A Hindi form shows नाम (nām). What information belongs on that line?

feedback.incorrect: Point to नाम and say name once.

lessons.title: Two people, two known practice names
lessons.gloss: select one already-practised name from a nonverbal identity cue

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Read both names from the earlier sentence work:
मीरा, अरुण.

blocks.title: The two words — attach one nonverbal cue to each person

segments.text: For this closed practice bank only:
A becomes मीरा.
B becomes अरुण.
Look for five seconds. Cover the Devanagari names. Point to A and recall its name; point to B and recall its name. Uncover and compare.

blocks.title: Guided Practice — select, do not copy

segments.text: With the bank visible, choose the value requested by B, then the value requested by A. Do not write either one. This pass separates selection from spelling.
Stop after the two-way contrast. No third name enters this field bank.

segments.prompt: In this practice bank, select the Devanagari name paired with B.

feedback.incorrect: Reveal A becomes मीरा and B becomes अरुण, point to B, then cover the bank again.

lessons.title: Fill one field with the bank visible
lessons.gloss: complete one Hindi name field with a visible two-value bank

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Read the label नाम (nām). Recall the visible bank: A मीरा, B अरुण.
Keep the bank visible. Card A requests its known value:
Select मीरा and copy it on the line. Read the completed field from label to value. This is supported entry, not independent writing evidence.

blocks.title: Writing — separate spelling and placement passes

segments.text: First check only spelling: मी | रा. Then check one ordinary space after the colon. If one dimension differs, repair that dimension and stop.
Stop after one supported field.

segments.prompt: With the two-value bank visible, complete the Hindi name field for A.

feedback.incorrect: Use the visible bank, select A becomes मीरा, then repair spelling or placement in separate passes.

lessons.title: Hide the bank, then fill one line
lessons.gloss: complete one requested Hindi name field after the answer bank is hidden

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Look once: A मीरा, B अरुण. Cover the complete bank and wait ten seconds.
Keep the bank hidden. Complete only this field:
The requested value comes from memory; there is no copyable answer beside the line. Reveal the bank only after writing.
Compare in order: (1) requested person, (2) four written positions, (3) vowel marks and headline, (4) spacing after the colon. Repair the first differing dimension and stop.
This is one delayed choice, not the published six-field A1 form.

segments.prompt: After hiding the bank for ten seconds, complete नाम (nām) for B. Do not reveal the bank until the attempt is finished.

feedback.correct: The hidden-bank cue selected अरुण independently.
feedback.incorrect: Reveal the bank now, then compare selection, spelling, vowel marks, and spacing in separate passes.

lessons.title: One no-model Hindi name field
lessons.gloss: choose and write one known Hindi name from a nonverbal cue with no model

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Close the preceding lessons. Keep only the two learned identity symbols in memory. There is no Devanagari value bank, support-language name, romanization, or completed model below.
Complete the requested field:
Choose the known value attached to A and write it from memory. Do not open an earlier lesson until the attempt is complete.
After writing, compare in four bounded passes: requested person, spelling, vowel marks/headline, then label-value placement. Repair only the first differing dimension.

This completes one field pattern. Five field families remain before the published six-to-eight-item A1 practical-form task can be attempted. This one-field checkpoint is untimed and does not claim full A1 readiness.

segments.prompt: With no bank, romanization, or copyable answer, complete the Hindi name field for A.

feedback.correct: The nonverbal cue independently selected मीरा.
feedback.incorrect: Finish the attempt first; then reopen the bank and repair selection, spelling, vowel marks, or placement in separate passes.
